description: The SSE frames agent streams to chat from POST /ask when `stream` is true. Emitted by agent and hand-parsed by chat; each side previously pinned its own copy of this shape in its own tests, so a rename passed both suites. Frames arrive as `data: <json>\n\n` -- the transport framing is chat's own concern, these are the decoded bodies.

rules.wireNames: The `done` frame's `citations` and `usage` are Python dataclass `__dict__` dumps, so an attribute rename in app/citations.py or loop.py silently renames a wire key with no serializer in between.
rules.answer: `answer` on the terminal frame -- not the concatenated tokens -- is authoritative. The two differ when the loop strips hallucinated citation markers, or when a hop streams a preamble before calling a tool. A consumer that falls back to the tokens shows text the agent already rejected.
rules.ordering: Zero or more `token` frames, then exactly one terminal frame. A stream that ends without one is a failed answer, not an empty one.

cases.name: a single-hop answer, streamed then finalised
a citation with no heading keeps the key and nulls it
a tool hop streams a preamble, so the tokens are not the answer
cases.$comment: The reason `answer` exists. Concatenating the tokens here yields the preamble too.

cases.name: the loop gives up and says so

frames.answer: I don't know based on the available data.

tolerated.name: a frame type the consumer does not know
tolerated.reason: Chat ignores it rather than failing the stream, so agent can add a frame kind without a lockstep release.

tolerated.name: a terminal frame from an agent too old to send `answer`
tolerated.reason: Absent, not null. The consumer falls back to the accumulated tokens -- degraded but not broken.

tolerated.name: a terminal frame carrying only what chat reads
tolerated.reason: `retrieved_ids`, `usage`, `idk`, `decision`, `tool_calls` and `hallucinated_citations` are emitted but parsed by no consumer, so a frame without them is still valid.

consumed.$comment: What chat's AgentFrame actually reads. Everything else on a `done` frame is written by agent and read by nobody -- pinned here as observation, not contract.
